import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as stats

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

# Check the first few rows of the dataset
df.head()

# Check the unique habitat types
unique_habitats = df['habitat'].unique()
print("Unique habitat types:", unique_habitats)

# Group the data by habitat and calculate the mean and standard deviation of 'n.gard'
grouped_data = df.groupby('habitat')['n.gard'].agg(['mean', 'std']).reset_index()
print("Grouped data by habitat:", grouped_data)

# Perform a one-way ANOVA to test for significant differences in 'n.gard' across habitats
anova_result = stats.f_oneway(*[group['n.gard'] for name, group in df.groupby('habitat')])
print("ANOVA result:", anova_result)

# Visualize the data using a boxplot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.boxplot(x='habitat', y='n.gard', data=df)
plt.title('Prevalence of Non-Native Plants Introduced via Gardening by Habitat Type')
plt.xlabel('Habitat Type')
plt.ylabel('Count of Non-Native Plants Introduced via Gardening')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
